Soccer Analytics: Key Figures by Stage

Results come from the pipeline (targets::tar_make() in the project root); this report only reads and plots them. Each figure is also saved as a PNG in figures/ (in the project root) for slides. The Understat figures (stage 0) live in the earlier tweedie_fit.Rmd and nbg_fit.Rmd.

library(targets)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
tar_source()
team_match <- tar_read(team_match)
stage1 <- tar_read(stage1)
shots <- tar_read(shots)

Stage 1: team level

1.1 Team attacking profiles. Each point is a team’s season. Teams reach their xG through volume, quality, or both.

save_fig(plot_team_profiles(team_match), "1-1_team_profiles", 8, 6)

1.2 Five estimates of the Tweedie index. If team xG were a single compound Poisson-gamma, these would agree.

save_fig(plot_p_compare(stage1), "1-2_p_compare", 8, 4)

show_table(p_compare_table(stage1))
Estimate p 95% interval Gap from fitted p (in fitted-p SEs)
Tweedie fit 1.487 1.328 to 1.645 0.0
Volume elasticity (2 - e) 1.394 1.354 to 1.433 -1.1
Quality elasticity (1 + e) 1.392 1.345 to 1.439 -1.2
Shot shape (moments) 1.635 - 1.8
Shot shape (MLE) 1.494 - 0.1

1.3 Calibration of the two-part model. Predicted shots x predicted quality against actual team-match xG; decile means on the diagonal mean calibrated.

save_fig(plot_calibration(team_match, stage1$pred_nbg, stage1$cal_nbg), "1-3_calibration", 6, 6)

1.4 Why only open-play shots. Goal rate against mean xG within xG deciles. Direct free kicks sit above the diagonal: StatsBomb’s xG underrates them.

save_fig(plot_xg_reliability(tar_read(shots_all)), "1-4_xg_calibration_by_type", 7, 5)

Stage 1: shot quality

1.5 Distribution of xG per shot. The three-component mixture (solid) and its components (dashed).

save_fig(plot_shape(shots, stage1), "1-5_shot_quality_mixture", 8, 5)

1.6 Where each kind of shot comes from. The high-value tail is close-range and central; the long-range cluster is outside the box.

save_fig(plot_shot_map(shots), "1-6_shot_map_by_component", 10, 4.5)

show_table(component_profile(shots))
component n share median_xg median_distance pct_header pct_first_time goal_rate goals_over_xg
1 1713 0.048 0.0070 34.5 0.004 0.159 0.009 1.33
2 30400 0.851 0.0475 19.3 0.182 0.318 0.063 1.01
3 3619 0.101 0.3500 8.9 0.156 0.528 0.416 1.04

Stage 2: stints and identification

2.1 Stint lengths. Short stints are common, but most minutes are played in long stints with the starting lineups intact, which is the source of the collinearity.

save_fig(plot_stint_lengths(tar_read(stints)), "2-1_stint_lengths", 7, 4)

2.2 Teammate overlap. Share of the lower-minute player’s time spent on the pitch with the other, for outfield players with 900+ minutes.

save_fig(plot_overlap(tar_read(overlap)), "2-2_teammate_overlap", 7, 4)

2.3 Precision of player effects. Most players’ standard errors exceed the entire spread of team attacking effects.

save_fig(plot_player_se(tar_read(precision)), "2-3_player_se", 8, 4.5)

2.4 Game state. Shot rates by score and time remaining, from the segment table; this is why stage 3b controls for time.

save_fig(plot_game_state(tar_read(segment_table)), "2-4_game_state", 8, 4.5)

Stage 3: player models

3.1 Held-out deviance by prior SD. Both player models dip below the team-only line (dotted) at small prior SDs.

cv3 <- tar_read(cv3)
save_fig(plot_cv_curve(cv3), "3-1_cv_curve", 8, 4)

show_table(cv_table(cv3))
Model Description Prior SD (% shots per 90) Held-out deviance Improvement over M0 Improvement over M1 Improvement over M3
M0 League, home, game state - 25,721.4 - - -
M1 M0 + teams - 24,447.2 1,274.2 (SE 113.8) - -
M2 M0 + players (ridge) 4.3 24,305.8 1,415.6 (SE 66.4) 141.4 (SE 55.0) -
M3 M0 + teams + players (ridge) 3.5 24,337.5 1,383.9 (SE 95.4) 109.7 (SE 31.2) -

3.2 Split-half reliability. M3 fit separately on odd and even matches.

save_fig(plot_split_half(tar_read(split_half3)), "3-2_split_half", 9, 4.5)

3.3 Player effects by position. Group means shift a little; individual spread is much larger.

save_fig(plot_effects_by_position(tar_read(effects3), tar_read(positions)),
         "3-3_effects_by_position", 8, 4.5)

Stage 3b: time controls and positional prior

3b.1 Position effects with and without time controls. If the filled points sit closer to zero than the open ones, the positional pattern was mostly substitution timing.

save_fig(plot_position_comparison(tar_read(position_fx)), "3b-1_position_effects", 9, 4.5)

3b.2 Held-out deviance, including the positional prior (M4).

save_fig(plot_cv_curve(cv3b), "3b-2_cv_curve", 8, 4)
